::: {.hero-banner}
# Synthetic panels with causal structure you can inspect

`pypanelsim` generates balanced panel data while keeping assignment, untreated
potential outcomes, treatment effects, observed covariates, and latent unit
features explicit. Every draw is reproducible, validated, and estimator-neutral.
:::

## Start with a canonical design

```python
import pypanelsim as pps

panel = pps.classic_factor(overlap=1.0, seed=42)
y, w = panel.as_arrays()

print(panel.shape)       # (200, 50)
print(panel.true_att)    # 1.1
```

## Or compose the assignment law

```python
simulator = pps.PanelSimulator(
    name="observed_selection",
    dimensions=pps.PanelDimensions(120, 48),
    feature_model=pps.GaussianUnitFeatures(2, 2),
    assignment=pps.BinaryLogitAssignment(
        adoption_period=32,
        intercept=-1.1,
        observable_coefficients=(1.2, -0.8),
        unobservable_coefficients=(0.0, 0.0),
    ),
    outcome_model=my_outcome_model,
    effect_model=pps.LinearRampEffect(0.12),
)
```

The same shared features reach assignment and the untreated-outcome model.
Observed features are exposed to downstream estimators; latent features remain
simulation truth.

## Installation

```bash
uv add "pypanelsim @ git+ssh://git@github.com/apoorvalal/pypanelsim.git"
```

Install the documentation and estimator interoperability stack with:

```bash
uv sync --extra docs
```
